changeSet.author: hephaestus

preConditions.sqlCheck: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'ck_login_provider_type' AND pg_get_constraintdef(oid) LIKE '%OIDC%'

changeSet.comment: A login provider can be of the type OIDC. This release reads the type, and the next release writes it, so a server of the previous release never meets it. The previous release writes only the old values, so it runs beside the wider check. NOT VALID replaces the check without a table scan. The lock timeout fails the step fast behind a long transaction, so that it can run again. A rerun finds the wider check and marks it ran.
changeSet.sql: SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'; ALTER TABLE login_provider DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS ck_login_provider_type, ADD CONSTRAINT ck_login_provider_type CHECK (type IN ('GITHUB', 'GITLAB', 'OIDC', 'OUTLINE', 'SLACK')) NOT VALID

rollback.sql: SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'; ALTER TABLE login_provider DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS ck_login_provider_type, ADD CONSTRAINT ck_login_provider_type CHECK (type IN ('GITHUB', 'GITLAB', 'OUTLINE', 'SLACK')) NOT VALID

changeSet.author: hephaestus
changeSet.comment: Validation reads every row of login_provider without blocking reads or writes. Each stored row met the narrower check, so it meets this one. Validating a valid check again does nothing.
changeSet.sql: SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'; ALTER TABLE login_provider VALIDATE CONSTRAINT ck_login_provider_type
